problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $p(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
f(-3)=-6,\,{f}^{′}(-3)=2,\,p(-3)=-5,\,{p}^{′}(-3)=-3
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)+p(x))$ at $x=-3.$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Linear Combination of Functions Given the Necessary Data
examples.problem:
The values of functions $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=-3$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $p(x)$ | $q(x)$ | $p'(x)$ | $q'(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-3$ | $1$ | $8$ | $0$ | $-2$ |

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( p(x) + 5q(x) \big)$ at $x=-3.$
examples.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( p(x) + 5q(x) \right) = p'(x) + 5q'(x).
$$

At the point where $x=-3$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(p(x)+5q(x))|}_{x=-3} & ={p}^{′}(-3)+5{q}^{′}(-3) \\  & =0+5\cdot (-2) \\  & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=0$ are given in the table below. 

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $2\pi $ | $\pi $ | $\pi $ | $0$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=0,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(0)g(0)-f(0){g}^{′}(0)}{(g(0))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\pi \cdot \pi -2\pi \cdot 0}{{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
